christe caelorum habitator: O Christ, kind dweller in the heavens,
life of the saints, their way, their hope and their salvation,
receive in your mercy the offering
of praise we make to you.
The choir of all the angels ever
blesses you in the heavens on high,
By the merits of the holy Virgin Mary
and of all the faithful alike,
hold back, O loving Lord, the punishment we deserve,
Grant that we may celebrate your praise here,
so that, faithful to you, we may go on with it
in heaven, singing to the Trinity
christe pastorum caput: O Christ, head and prince of shepherds,
your faithful people, glad to keep this feast,
sing to you in sacred song
the praises that are your due.
Making him your chosen minister
and joining him to your priesthood, you gave him
to stand by your people as a faithful leader
and a good provider.
He was the guide and pattern of the flock,
a light to the blind, a relief to the wretched,
a provident father to all,
made all things to all.
O Christ, who give in heaven the crown deserved
to your saints, make us follow this master
in our lives with docile hearts, and at the last
come to an end like his.
Let equal praise extol the Father most high
and you, O Saviour, loving King, for ever;
let the glory of the Holy Spirit resound
through all the world. Amen.

Look upon us, our defender,

To you, O Christ, most loving King,

dum sacerdotum celebrant: While the faithful keep the feasts of the priests
with solemn worship and reverence,

O High Priest.
By your gift the fathers were able

to rule them by holy lives, and by the word

Nor could adversity move them

for the sure hope of the rewards to come

So, when the labours of this frail life

The highest honour of glory and praise

let all that is celebrate you

sacrata nobis gaudia: The yearly day has brought back to us

See, for the keeping of the flock

wholesome pasture.
They drive the wolves from its borders,
they chase the robbers far away,
they fill the sheep with richness,
they never desert the fold.
Now that you possess such joys,
most holy leaders of the flocks,
ask grace for us
before the judge's throne.
Eternal Christ, High Priest,
to you be equal glory
with the Father and the loving Spirit,
for ever and ever. Amen.
o sator rerum: O Maker of all things, restorer of the ages,

author of light.

resound through all the world. Amen.

aeterne lucis conditor: Eternal Maker of light,
yourself all light and day,
who know no night at all,
being by nature light everlasting,
now the pale night gives way
to the coming of the day;
dimming the light of the stars,
the bright morning star is here.
Now we rise gladly from our beds,
singing our thanks to you,
because the sun, bringing back the day,
has overcome the blind night.
Now, holy one, we pray,
let not the pleasures of the flesh creep in with their soft heat,
nor our mind give way
to the snares of the world.
Let anger not stir up quarrels,
nor the belly provoke gluttony,
nor hunger for wealth pervert us,
nor shameful excess take hold of us.
But sober, with steady mind
and remaining chaste in body,
let us spend this whole day
for Christ with faithful spirit.
Grant this, most loving Father,
and you, the Only-begotten, equal to the Father,
with the Spirit, the Paraclete,
reigning through every age. Amen.
o lux beata: O blessed light of the saints in heaven
and highest hope of mortals,
Jesus, on whom at your birth
the love of a home smiled;
Mary, rich in grace,
who alone could hold Jesus
to your chaste breast,
giving him kisses with your milk;
and you, chosen from the fathers of old
as guardian of the Virgin,
whom the divine Child calls
by the sweet name of father:
born of the noble stock of Jesse
for the salvation of the nations,
hear us, who in supplication
pour out our prayers from the heart.
The grace of every virtue
with which your home flourished,
may it be given us to show
in the ways of our own homes.
Jesus, who were made obedient
to your parents,
with the Father most high and the Spirit
glory be to you for ever. Amen.
audit tyrannus anxius: The tyrant hears in anguish
that the Prince of kings has come,
who is to rule the name of Israel
and hold the throne of David.
Beside himself, he cries out at the news:
“A successor is upon us, we are driven out;
go, soldier, seize the sword,
drench the cradles with blood!”
What does such a crime achieve?
What does his wickedness gain Herod?
Alone among so many deaths
Christ is carried away unharmed.
Hail, flowers of the martyrs,
whom on the very threshold of light
the persecutor of Christ cut down,
as a whirlwind the budding roses.
You, the first victims for Christ,
tender flock of the slain,
in your innocence beneath the very altar
you play with palms and crowns.
Jesus, to you be glory,
who were born of the Virgin,
with the Father and the life-giving Spirit,
for ever and ever. Amen.
deus tuorum militum: O God, of your soldiers
the portion, crown and reward,
as we sing the praises of your martyr,
loose us from the bond of sin.
This witness spoke with the mouth
what the heart’s treasury believed;
by following Christ he found him
in the shedding of his blood.
Rightly counting the joys of the world
and its harmful allurements
as passing things,
he came to the things of heaven.
He ran bravely through his torments
and bore them manfully;
pouring out his blood for you,
he possesses eternal gifts.
Therefore with humble prayer
we ask you, most loving Lord:
in this triumph of your martyr
forgive your servants their guilt,
that we may share in his reward
and his company,
and rejoice for ever,
joined to him in the courts of heaven.
Praise and everlasting glory
to you, Father, with the Son
and with the holy Paraclete
for ever and ever. Amen.
dulce fit nobis: It is sweet for us
to remember the little
house of Nazareth and its poor way of life;
it is good to tell
in song the hidden life of Jesus.
In the craft of Joseph,
to be honoured though lowly,
Jesus grows up in hidden years,
and of his own will joins him
as his partner in a carpenter’s work.
Beside her gracious Son
sits his loving mother,
beside her husband sits the good wife,
happy if with her loving service
she can lighten the cares of the weary.
O you who were not without
work and toil,
nor unacquainted with hardship, help the wretched;
all who beg your support,
look on them with kindly face.
To you, Jesus, be honour and power,
who give us the holy
pattern of life,
and who with the Father most high
and the life-giving Spirit reign. Amen.
iesu redemptor saeculi: Jesus, Redeemer of the world,
Word of the Father most high,
light of the invisible light,
ever-watchful guardian of your own:
Maker of all things
and ordainer of the times,
refresh our bodies, weary with toil,
with the quiet of the night.
You who break the depths of hell,
deliver us from the enemy,
that he may not lead astray
those redeemed by your blood,
so that, while weighed down by the body
we remain here a short time,
our flesh may sleep
but our mind know no sleep.
Jesus, to you be glory,
who shine forth having conquered death,
with the Father and the life-giving Spirit,
for ever and ever. Amen.
